full_judgment: 4. Defendant No. 2, (appellant) went on appeal before the Court of District Judge, Jessore and the appeal was heard by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge). The appellate Court on the findings since consequential relief by way of confirmation of possession and a decree for permanent injunction have not been prayed for the suit is not maintainable; that plaintiffs having had admitted they are out of possession of a portion of the land (.36 acre) in suit and that said fact having been corroborated by the evidence of P.W. 4 their suit is not maintainable as they have not prayed for a decree for recovery of khas possession; that the land in suit is not identifiable; that Taru Rishi possessed the land in suit has not been proved by producing document; that in the background of the evidence on record the finding of the trial Court as regard possession of plaintiffs appears to be not correct and that plaintiffs have failed to prove by oral evidence that Taru Rishi was in possession of the land in suit and that after him they are in possession of the land in suit; that from the papers of the defendant it appears that he is in possession of the suit land since 1968 allowed the appeal and upon reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court dismissed the suit.
